children: By Summer Zhen

China's yuan edged lower against the US dollar on Friday even as the central bank lifted its daily midpoint guidance to a fresh more than four-year high, curbed by a firm greenback on growing expectations of near-term rate hikes.
Sentiment was also weighed by US President Donald Trump's new tariff threat.
The spot yuan
was 0.06% lower at 6.6652 to the dollar as of 0322 GMT,  after trading in a range of 6.6590 to 6.6661.
The yuan is on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, although by a modest margin.

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, supported by expectations of Federal Reserve policy tightening with some traders seeing a quarter-point interest rate hike on December 9.
Prior to the market opening, the People's Bank of China set the midpoint rate
at 6.7075 per dollar, its strongest since July 11, 2022, 471 pips weaker than a Reuters' estimate.
The spot yuan is allowed to trade a maximum of 2% on either side of the fixed midpoint each day.
The Trump administration proposed new maximum tariffs of 20% to 40% on 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan and the EU, threatening to pressure China's exports.
If tariffs head toward 40%, it will drive up global inflation, with the US dollar likely to benefit, Nanhua Futures analysts said in a note.
The yuan is down 0.2% against the dollar this month, and 4.9% firmer this year.
The yuan's appreciation this year has been largely driven by strong exports and exporters' FX settlement demand due to a strong trade surplus.
Some analysts remain positive on the yuan's outlook for next year.
BNP Paribas expects exporters' FX selling to remain robust next year, strengthening the yuan to 6.4 by year-end 2027.
The offshore yuan traded at 6.6661 yuan per dollar
, down about 0.07% in Asian trade.
The dollar's six-currency index
was at 103.68.
